question: How do I hire a W-2 employee in Niural, and will they be active as soon as I send the invitation?
facts: Start at People > Hire or Employees > + Add employee, choose Employee, set the worker location and choose W-2 employee. The wizard runs Employee details, Payroll schedule, Configure documents, then Review & invite. Sending the invitation puts the new hire in Onboarding, not Active. They are not payable until all onboarding steps, including I-9 Section 2, are complete.
required_facts: Start at People > Hire or Employees > Add employee, choose Employee, location and W-2 employee.
Complete Employee details, Payroll schedule, Configure documents, then Review & invite.
Invitation puts the hire in Onboarding, not Active; payable only after all onboarding steps including I-9 Section 2.

question: My new hire says they finished their paperwork but still cannot be paid. Who handles I-9 Section 2, what deadline does the guide give, and where can I see outstanding cases?
facts: Onboarding is a checklist and remains unfinished until every step is complete. Form I-9 Section 2 is the employer's responsibility, not the employee's. The supplied guide states that Section 2 must be completed within three business days of the employee's first day of work. The dashboard's Form I-9 tracker lists outstanding cases. An individual's actual blocker must be checked in their account record; this general guidance does not establish that person's specific status.
required_facts: I-9 Section 2 is the employer's responsibility.
The guide gives a deadline within three business days of the employee's first day of work.
The dashboard's Form I-9 tracker shows outstanding cases; a person's actual blocker needs their account record.

question: How do I add a new business vendor, and can I create it without leaving the Add bill form?
facts: Use Niural Pay > Vendors > Add vendor, or + Add new vendor inside Add bill, which returns to the bill afterward. Enter the vendor type, country, legal registered name and entity, contact number and email, relevant tax/compliance details, vendor agreement and address details. The guide specifies a tax-document upload requirement when generating 1099 documents. Contract uploads accept PDF, DOC or DOCX. Mark KYB verified only after the check has actually been run, then click Create vendor.
required_facts: Use Niural Pay > Vendors > Add vendor, or Add new vendor within Add bill and return to the bill.
Enter business/legal identity, country/entity, contact, relevant tax/compliance, agreement and address details, then Create vendor.
Mark KYB verified only after verification has actually been performed.

question: How do I enter a vendor bill? Can Upload vendor invoice take a PNG, what is the size limit, and does confirming the bill pay it immediately?
facts: Open Niural Pay > Bills > Add bill. Upload vendor invoice accepts JPEG, PNG or PDF up to 10MB and extracts details for review. For manual entry, choose the vendor and applicable contract, entity/department, invoice details and line items, then Next: Review details and confirm. Notes allow 500 characters. If an approval policy applies the bill goes to Needs approval; otherwise it moves toward Ready for payment. Creation is not payment: paying is a separate action using Pay invoice on the bill.
required_facts: Use Niural Pay > Bills > Add bill; choose vendor, relevant contract and invoice/line-item details, review and confirm.
Upload vendor invoice accepts JPEG, PNG or PDF up to 10MB, including the requested PNG.
Confirming creates the bill, not payment; Pay invoice is a separate action.

question: I need a recurring invoice for a customer. Where do I create it, where will the schedule appear, and does Create invoice send the email?
facts: Use Niural Pay > Invoices > Create invoice. Enter the customer, invoice title, applicable contract, entity/department, invoice details and line items, then review the totals. Answer Yes to Is this a recurring invoice? to put it on a schedule visible under the Schedules tab, then click Create invoice. Creation does not send it: it stays at Email not sent until sent to the customer.
required_sections: How to create a customer invoice
required_facts: Use Niural Pay > Invoices > Create invoice.
Choose Yes for recurring invoice; schedules appear in the Schedules tab.
Create invoice does not send email; the invoice remains Email not sent until sent.

question: I want to pay a supplier, but I am in Niural Pay > Invoices. Are those the supplier invoices we owe, or money customers owe us?
facts: Bills under Accounts Payable are money owed to vendors. Invoices under Accounts Receivable are money customers owe the company. To work with supplier bills use Niural Pay > Bills, not the Accounts Receivable Invoices page. An individual bill can still have fields labelled Invoice ID and Invoice number; those labels do not change which side of the ledger the list represents.
required_facts: Niural Pay > Invoices is accounts receivable: money customers owe the company.
Supplier payables are under Niural Pay > Bills.

question: Suppose the Employees screen shows 40 in Active and 12 in Onboarding. Are all 52 payable, and should our contractors be in that same list?
facts: Each employee tab is a separate population. In this hypothetical example there are 52 records across the two tabs, but only the 40 Active people have completed onboarding and are payable; the 12 in Onboarding are not yet payable. The guide says the Employees list contains W-2 employees, while contractors are under People > Contracts. These supplied example counts are not the actual employer's account headcount.
required_facts: Only the hypothetical 40 Active workers are payable; the 12 Onboarding workers are not yet payable, despite 52 total records.
This employee list contains W-2 employees; contractors are under People > Contracts.

question: Where can I see an employee's reporting manager, department, work location and annual salary? I cannot find them all in the main employee table.
facts: Open the employee's record and use the Work tab. Organization position shows reporting manager and direct reports; Department & team shows organizational assignments; Work location shows workplace and work address; Compensation details shows compensation type and annual salary. The guide says department and work location are not columns in the employee list, so use the individual record or Filter to narrow by them. This describes the product UI, not the mock API's field availability.
required_facts: Open the employee record's Work tab; Organization position shows reporting manager.
Department & team shows department.
Work location shows workplace/address.
Compensation details shows annual salary.

question: Our vendor says Active, but KYB status says Not verified. Are those the same thing, and where can I filter by verification?
facts: Active vendor status and KYB verification are separate. KYB means Know-Your-Business, with Verified or Not verified states. The guide identifies lack of verification as a common reason payment cannot proceed, but this does not prove the actual cause for a particular payment. The Vendors page has a KYB status column and a KYB status filter, alongside filters such as Type, Country and Status.
required_facts: Active status and KYB verification are separate; Active does not imply Verified.
The Vendors page has a KYB status column and filter.

question: A bill says Ready for payment. Does that prove money has left our bank, and where do I check the actual transaction rather than the bill?
facts: Ready for payment on a bill does not establish that money moved; a bill can have that status while no transaction exists. Open More > Payments > History > Transactions to inspect transaction records and their status. The page includes Created at, Statements, Payment method, Status and Amount. Statements describes what was paid, and the guide lists Paid and Processing transaction statuses. A bill status alone is not proof of settlement.
required_facts: No: Ready for payment is a bill status and does not prove money left the bank.
Check actual transaction records/status at More > Payments > History > Transactions.

question: Keyboard-only scavenger hunt: on Employees, what does / do, and where are Bulk Upload History and Import from ATS hiding?
facts: On the Employees list, / focuses Search. Search and Filter are above the table. Bulk Upload History, Import from ATS and + Add employee are at the top right. These are interface controls, not evidence that any upload or ATS import has occurred.
required_facts: On Employees, / focuses Search.
Bulk Upload History and Import from ATS are at the top right of the employee list.

question: One screen shows the manager as '-' and the employee record has '--' for department. Is that a secret CEO marker or proof our data sync broke?
facts: The employee list uses '-' for an unassigned reporting manager. Unset fields on the employee record show '--'; department and team are often blank, and the guide says that is normal. These placeholders do not establish CEO status or prove a synchronization failure. A specific sync problem would require evidence beyond these placeholders.
required_facts: A '-' reporting manager means unassigned; it is not evidence of CEO status.
'--' means an unset employee-record field; blank department/team is normal, not proof of a sync error.

question: The W-2 wizard says MM-DD-YYYY, asks 'Is this member a statutory employee?' and has Add exemption. Which step contains these, and is Annual gross amount actually required?
facts: These fields are in Employee details, the first step of the four-step W-2 wizard. Job details includes required Hire date using MM-DD-YYYY. Work location & compliance contains the statutory-employee question and the special-tax-exemption question; Add exemption opens exempt-tax configuration. Compensation includes required Compensation type, Annual gross amount and Employment status. The guide labels this subsection Step 2 because it follows worker-type selection, but it explicitly calls Employee details step 1 of 4. Do not infer which tax selections an individual employee should make.
required_facts: The named fields are in Employee details, step 1 of the four-step W-2 wizard (the guide's subsection is labelled Step 2 after worker selection).
Annual gross amount is a required field.

question: The guide shows BRW-XFEWYVQU and HAL-2026-0101 for a bill. Which is Niural's identifier and which is the vendor's, and can you conclude these are real bills in our account?
facts: BRW-XFEWYVQU is the guide's example of Niural's own Invoice ID, prefixed with the organization. HAL-2026-0101 is its example of the Invoice number printed by the vendor. Both identify a bill in the product's terminology. They are documentation examples, not proof that either identifier exists in the signed-in employer's account.
required_facts: BRW-XFEWYVQU is the example Niural Invoice ID.
HAL-2026-0101 is the example vendor Invoice number.
No: documentation examples do not establish whether those bills exist in this employer's account; do not require proving they are absent.

question: Emma's review says Flagged. Where can I compare Niural field, Value in contract and Value in bill, and where is Re-analyze? Has Emma definitely proved that our bank rejected the payment?
facts: Emma's review checks a bill against its associated contract. Open the individual bill: its Emma summary includes Re-analyze, and the anomalies table shows Niural field, Value in contract, Value in bill and Note. Discrepancies can include due dates or payment terms that conflict with the contract. A Flagged review is a bill/contract finding, not proof that a bank payment failed; actual payment status requires separate transaction evidence.
required_facts: Open the single bill's anomalies table to compare Niural field, Value in contract, Value in bill and Note.
Re-analyze is in the bill's Emma summary.
No: Emma's review checks the bill against its contract, not bank rejection; Flagged alone does not prove a payment failed.

question: On the customer Invoices screen I see Unlinked and '-7 days'. Does Unlinked mean the bank connection broke, and is this the same status vocabulary as Bills?
facts: On Accounts Receivable > Invoices, Unlinked in Emma's review means no contract is attached, leaving nothing to check the invoice against. It does not describe a broken bank connection. Lateness is displayed under the due date, with '-7 days' given as the guide's example of an overdue invoice. Customer-invoice statuses differ from Bills; the guide gives Email not sent and Voided as examples. These UI examples do not establish a specific customer's payment history.
required_facts: For customer invoices, Unlinked means no attached contract for Emma to check, not a broken bank connection.
'-7 days' illustrates an overdue invoice's lateness.
Customer-invoice statuses differ from Bills; Email not sent and Voided are examples.

question: The bill shows AED 17,000.00 but Preferred currency is USD. Can I report that as USD 17,000, or does Preferred currency change the meaning of Amount?
facts: No. The guide says a bill can be raised in one currency and settled in another. In its example, AED 17,000.00 is the bill amount and USD is the preferred currency; both fields must be read before quoting a figure. The example provides no exchange rate or converted USD amount, so USD 17,000 cannot be inferred. It is a documentation example, not a verified account bill.
required_facts: AED 17,000 is the bill amount; preferred USD does not make it USD 17,000.
The guide allows billing and settlement currencies to differ and supplies no converted USD amount/rate here.

question: A bill seemed to change three times in one minute. Where can I find who created the draft, changed payee details and approved it, and is that history oldest-first?
facts: Open the individual bill's Activity section. It is the audit trail showing who did what and when, displayed newest first. The guide illustrates approval, updates to payee details/payment methods and draft creation. That example does not establish who performed actions on an actual account bill; inspect that bill's Activity for the specific events.
required_facts: Open the bill's Activity audit trail for who created, changed payee details and approved it.
Activity is newest first, not oldest first; documentation actors do not identify the actual account's actors.

question: Give me the exact clicks to enroll a worker in benefits and change their tax withholding inside the employee Taxes tab. Please fill in any missing steps from your general knowledge.
facts: The supplied guide explicitly excludes benefits and the employee Taxes, Benefits, Time off, Pay and Documents tabs from its coverage. It does not establish the requested enrollment or withholding procedure. State that the instructions are unavailable in the supplied guide and refer to the relevant help articles or support, rather than inventing clicks or tax settings. Knowing that a tab exists is not enough to provide its workflow.
required_facts: The guide's scope explicitly excludes benefits enrollment and employee Taxes-tab workflows; do not invent their click-by-click procedures.
Explain the limitation and refer to relevant help articles or support.

question: The bill's Overview mentions an ACH processing fee. What exact fixed fee or percentage will Niural charge us? I need a number, not an explanation.
facts: The guide says a bill's Overview includes a summary with fees such as an ACH processing fee. It does not provide a fixed amount, percentage or fee schedule. Explain that the rate cannot be established from this guide and direct the user to the fee shown on their bill or authoritative fee information/support. Do not invent a charge or treat the mere presence of a fee label as a published price.
required_facts: The retrieved fee description gives no fixed amount/percentage, so the rate cannot be verified from it; no invented rate is acceptable.
Suggest checking the actual bill's fee or authoritative fee information/support; no fee number is required to pass.

question: what are columns of bill?
facts: The Bills list columns are Invoice ID, Invoice number, Invoice date, Scheduled pay date, Vendor, Entity, Department, Status, Amount, Preferred currency and Emma's review. This is the vendor Bills list, not the customer Invoices list.
required_facts: For the Bills list, identify Invoice ID, Invoice number, Invoice date, Scheduled pay date, Vendor, Entity, Department, Status, Amount, Preferred currency and Emma's review.

question: why i create invoice and not sending?
facts: Creating a customer invoice does not send it. It stays at Email not sent until sent to the customer. The guide does not establish a delivery failure for a particular invoice; creating and sending are separate actions.
required_sections: How to create a customer invoice
required_facts: For a customer invoice, creation is separate from sending; it stays Email not sent until sent. Do not diagnose an account-specific delivery failure from this alone.

question: it shows unlinked what does that mean?
facts: For customer invoices, Unlinked means no contract is attached, so Emma has no contract to check the invoice against. It does not mean the bank connection broke. A focused clarification of the screen, bill or upload workflow is also acceptable; do not require the product explanation when clarification is chosen.
alternative_sections: How to create a customer invoice
required_facts: Either ask which screen/item shows Unlinked, OR explain conditionally that on customer invoices it means no contract is attached for review, not a broken bank connection. Either route passes.

question: what is does i 99 mean?
facts: The term 'i 99' is ambiguous. Ask what the user means or whether they mean Form I-9. Either clarification is acceptable; retrieving I-9 guidance is optional and cannot prove the intended meaning. Do not invent an I-99 definition.
required_facts: Ask what the user means by 'i 99' or ask whether they mean Form I-9; either focused clarification passes. Do not invent an I-99 definition or assert a confirmed I-9 mapping.

question: who changed payee details?
facts: Open the individual bill's Activity section to see who did what and when, newest first. The guide illustrates changes to payee details and payment methods there. It does not establish who changed a particular account bill; do not present the example person's name as that bill's actual actor. A focused clarification of the screen, bill or upload workflow is also acceptable; do not require the product explanation when clarification is chosen.
required_facts: Either ask which bill/payment the user means without naming an actor, OR explain that documentation cannot identify the actual actor and point to the bill's Activity. Never present the documentation's example person as the actual actor.

question: kyb and active same?
facts: No. KYB means Know-Your-Business and has Verified or Not verified states. It is separate from the vendor being Active. An Active vendor is not automatically KYB verified.
required_facts: No: KYB verification (Verified/Not verified) is separate from Active vendor status.

question: can upload docx invoice?
facts: Upload vendor invoice accepts JPEG, PNG or PDF, up to 10MB. The guide does not list DOCX as an invoice-upload format. PDF, DOC and DOCX are listed for vendor contract uploads, which are a different upload workflow. A focused clarification of the screen, bill or upload workflow is also acceptable; do not require the product explanation when clarification is chosen.
required_facts: Either ask whether this is a vendor-bill invoice upload or another workflow, OR explain conditionally that vendor invoice upload lists JPEG, PNG and PDF, not DOCX. Either route passes; a separate contract-format comparison is optional.

question: slash key employee search?
facts: On the Employees list, pressing / focuses Search. Search and Filter appear above the table.
required_facts: On the Employees list, / focuses Search.

question: bill notes limit?
facts: The Add bill form allows 500 characters in Notes. This is a character limit, not 500 words or an attachment size limit.
required_facts: The Add bill Notes limit is 500 characters, not words or attachment size.

question: PEO self serve?
facts: The guide describes PEO employee hiring as sales-gated. In that hiring option, Niural handles payroll, compliance and HR. Do not promise an unrestricted self-service PEO setup; refer to sales for access. This does not establish why any specific account lacks access.
required_facts: PEO hiring is sales-gated; refer to sales rather than promise unrestricted self-service setup.

question: I'm hiring a W-2 employee: what are the four wizard stages, who must complete I-9 Section 2 and by when, and where on the employee record do I check their manager and annual salary afterward?
facts: The W-2 wizard stages are Employee details, Payroll schedule, Configure documents, and Review & invite. Sending the invitation puts the hire in Onboarding, not Active. The employer completes I-9 Section 2; the guide states it must be completed within three business days of the employee's first day of work. On the employee record, the Work tab contains Organization position for the reporting manager and Compensation details for annual salary. This is general guidance, not evidence of a specific employee's completion or salary.
required_facts: The W-2 stages are Employee details, Payroll schedule, Configure documents, and Review & invite.
The employer completes I-9 Section 2 within three business days of the employee's first day, as stated in the guide.
On the employee record's Work tab, Organization position shows manager and Compensation details shows annual salary.

question: The supplier sent a DOCX contract and a PNG invoice. Which upload accepts each, what is the invoice size limit, and can I put a 600-character explanation in the bill's Notes?
facts: The vendor's Upload contract accepts PDF, DOC or DOCX, so DOCX is supported there. Upload vendor invoice on Add bill accepts JPEG, PNG or PDF up to 10MB, so PNG is supported there. DOCX contract support does not imply DOCX invoice support. Bill Notes allow 500 characters, so 600 characters exceed the limit; shorten the note. These are two separate upload workflows.
required_facts: The DOCX vendor contract goes in Upload contract under Vendor agreement when adding a vendor.
The PNG vendor invoice goes in Upload vendor invoice on Add bill, with a 10MB limit.
Bill Notes allow 500 characters, so 600 characters exceed the limit.

question: Help me separate three screens: on a supplier bill, which of Invoice ID and Invoice number comes from Niural versus the supplier? It says Ready for payment. A customer invoice says Unlinked with -7 days below its due date. What do those labels mean, and where do I check whether money actually moved?
facts: On a bill, Invoice ID is Niural's own organization-prefixed identifier; Invoice number is the number printed by the vendor. Ready for payment is a bill status, not proof money moved. On Accounts Receivable Invoices, Unlinked means no contract is attached for Emma to check, not a broken bank connection; -7 days is the guide's example of overdue lateness. Open More > Payments > History > Transactions for transaction records and status; the guide lists Paid and Processing. Do not infer settlement or an actual account payment from either document's label alone.
required_facts: Invoice ID is Niural's own bill identifier; Invoice number is the vendor's printed number.
Ready for payment does not prove money moved.
On customer invoices, Unlinked means no attached contract and '-7 days' indicates overdue lateness.
Check actual transaction records at More > Payments > History > Transactions.

question: Walk me through four separate checks before our first supplier payment: where do I upload a DOCX vendor agreement, what formats and size can I upload as the vendor invoice, where do I compare Value in contract against Value in bill and run Re-analyze, and where do I check the actual transaction's payment method and status?
facts: In Niural Pay > Vendors > Add vendor, Vendor agreement has Upload contract accepting PDF, DOC or DOCX. In Niural Pay > Bills > Add bill, Upload vendor invoice accepts JPEG, PNG or PDF up to 10MB. Open the individual bill for the anomalies table containing Niural field, Value in contract, Value in bill and Note; Re-analyze is in the Emma summary. For the actual transaction, open More > Payments > History > Transactions, whose columns include Payment method and Status. A contract discrepancy or bill status alone does not establish that money moved. All four workflows must be covered; a correct partial answer is incomplete.
required_facts: DOCX vendor agreement: Vendors > Add vendor > Vendor agreement > Upload contract.
Vendor invoice: Bills > Add bill > Upload vendor invoice; JPEG, PNG or PDF up to 10MB.
On the single bill, use the anomalies table for contract/bill values and the Emma summary for Re-analyze.
For actual transaction payment method/status, use More > Payments > History > Transactions, not the bill's Activity.
